1.1: This letter is sent from Paul, prisoner of Jesus Christ, and from our brother Timothy, to Philemon, our good friend and co-worker;
1.2: to our sister Apphia, to Archippus who fights alongside us, and to your house church.
1.3: May you have grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: I always thank my God for you, remembering you in my prayers,
1.5: because I hear of your trust in the Lord Jesus and your love for all believers.
1.6: I pray that you will put the generous nature of your trust in God into action as you recognize all the good things we share in Christ.
1.7: Your love, my dear brother ,has brought me much happiness and encouragement. You have really inspired those of us who believe!
1.8: That's why even though I'm brave enough in Christ to order you to do your duty,
1.9: I would rather ask you this favor out of love. Old Paul, now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus,
1.10: is appealing to you on behalf of Onesimus who became my adopted son during my imprisonment.
1.11: In the past he was of no use to you, but now he's useful to both you and me!
1.12: I send him to you with my fondest wishes.
1.13: I'd have preferred to keep him here with me so that he could have helped me as you would have done while I am in chains for telling the good news.
1.14: But I decided not to do anything without your permission. I didn't want you to be forced to do good, but to do so willingly.
1.15: Maybe you lost him for a while so that you could have him back forever!
1.16: He's not a servant anymore, because he's more than a servant. He's a specially-loved brother ,particularly to me, and even more to you, both as a man and as a fellow-believer in the Lord.
1.17: So if you consider me as a colleague working together with you for the Lord, welcome him as if you were welcoming me.
1.18: If he has done you any wrong, or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
1.19: I Paul am signing this with my own hand: I will repay you. Of course I won't mention what you owe me, including your very self!
1.20: Yes, brother ,I'm expecting this favor from you in the Lord; please make me happy in Christ.
1.21: I'm writing about this to you because I'm convinced you'll do as I ask—in fact I know you'll do even more than I've asked!
1.22: In the meantime please have a room ready for me, for I hope to be able to return to see you soon in answer to your prayers.
1.23: Epaphras who is here in prison with me sends his greetings,
1.24: as do my co-workers Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke.
1.25: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.
